pull_request.body:
## [P1/S-06] Hooks: session start, bash and edit guards, git hooks
**Done when:** `slicekit hook pre-bash` denies a commit on `main`, a push to `main`, a force push, a commit touching a frozen intake snapshot, a destructive command from config, and `git commit`/`git push`/`gh pr` writes while a subagent marker is active; allows everything else; denies with "could not read hook input" on bad stdin · `slicekit hook pre-edit` denies an edit to a frozen test of the active slice, a new file under the docs root while the slice is `tests-red` or `building` (except the runbook), and any edit to `.slicekit/{journal.log,baselines,state}` · `slicekit hook session-start` prints divergence and the active slice, re-injects the handoff and brief on `compact`, and exits 0 with no network · `init` installs `.githooks/prepare-commit-msg` and `pre-commit`; a commit on `slice/P1-S-06-x` gains `Slice: P1/S-06`; `check` gains the `hooks` and `trailer` rules.
**Proof:** `npm test` → `# tests 551 / # pass 551 / # fail 0` on Windows 11, Node 22.19.0 · `node bin/slicekit.js check` → `check: 0 findings, 0 over baseline, 0 blocking, 10 rules` · five task reviews and seven re-reviews or controller probe runs, all on Opus; one whole-branch review that drove the full install end to end (every registered hook answered through the command `.claude/settings.json` registers) and ran the 22 commands the build loop needs in the main session (none refused); one fix wave, verified with a fresh-repo and cross-worktree probe
**Decisions:** every hook runs through one dispatcher: guards (`pre-bash`, `pre-edit`, `stop`, `subagent-stop`) refuse on unreadable input, a crash, a non-plain-object or unserialisable answer, a timeout (the kit's hook timeout minus 2 s) or a handler that never settles; informational hooks step aside with `{}`; the answer is always one JSON line at exit 0, and a guard not built yet allows, so installing the kit never blocks a team early · `pre-bash` judges parsed commands segment by segment: shell keywords, wrappers (`timeout`, `nice`, `xargs`, `nohup`…), `bash -c`, here-documents, `git -C`/`cd`/`pushd` targets (Git Bash `/c/` paths mapped on Windows), and branch switches earlier in the same line; a directory it cannot resolve refuses a commit or an unqualified push · the destructive list matches parsed commands with quoted content kept, skipping readers (`echo`, `grep`, `git log`…) and commit messages; the default `TRUNCATE` pattern now needs `TABLE`, and the force-push pattern is gone because the parsed force-push rule covers it · from a subagent every `gh pr` subcommand except `view|list|status|checks|diff` is refused, and `gh api` with a non-GET method · `cherry-pick`, `revert` and `am` count as commits on a protected branch; `merge`, `pull` and `rebase` do not · `pre-edit` judges a file by its own repository root (the deeper of its nearest config and its git top level), canonicalises Windows short names and refuses stream names · `session-start` fetches with an explicit refspec so its counts are never stale without saying so, caps the handoff at 4,000 characters and prefixes every handoff line so state-file text cannot impersonate the hook · `prepare-commit-msg` puts `Slice:` first in the message's final trailer block; `init` sets `core.hooksPath` only when it is unset, never overwrites a team's own hook, and warns about hooks in `.git/hooks` that stop running.
**Runbook:** no operational change: the kit has no runtime yet.
**Infra / migration:** none. After this merges, the kit's own main checkout refuses direct commits on `main` (its `core.hooksPath` is now `.githooks`); set `ALLOW_PROTECTED_COMMIT=1` for a deliberate exception.
**Try it:** 1. In the checkout: `echo '{"session_id":"s","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git push origin main"},"cwd":"."}' | node bin/slicekit.js hook pre-bash` → a deny naming `main`. 2. The same with `"command":"grep -rn truncate src"` → `{}`. 3. `echo '{"session_id":"s","source":"startup","cwd":"."}' | node bin/slicekit.js hook session-start` → divergence and active-slice lines.
**Reviewer blocked:** Task 1: a guard allowed when its handler returned nothing, a non-object, or something that did not print as a decision; a late error made the process exit 1 (fixed over two rounds) · Task 2: commits on main got through inside `if`/`for`, behind `timeout`/`xargs`, through Git Bash paths and after `git checkout main`; a subagent could approve its own PR; `grep truncate` and here-document bodies were refused; round two caught `<<<`, arithmetic shifts and checkout-of-a-file regressions (all fixed) · Task 3: an edit in another worktree was judged by the session's repository; Windows short names and stream names reached frozen files; Edit could create a document (fixed) · Task 4: stale counts when the fetch refspec missed the default branch; an unbounded handoff that could forge hook lines (fixed) · Task 5: the trailer rule read trailers differently from git; cherry-pick, revert, rebase and a clean merge reached main; Windows teams got a blocking finding with no remedy; a stale origin made the rule judge other people's commits (fixed over two rounds) · Whole-branch: hooks staged non-executable in a fresh Windows repo; the subagent marker was keyed to one worktree (both fixed, with seven minors)
**Should-haves declined:** none (recorded as known limits: `git am` onto a protected branch has no hook; a pull with rebase on a main that carries local commits is refused unless `ALLOW_PROTECTED_COMMIT=1`; and in `src/hooks/pre-bash.js`: variables, `eval`, aliases and shell functions are not expanded; `echo '…' | bash`; `--git-dir`/`GIT_DIR` pointing at another repository; SQL inside a file (`psql -f`); `gh api` with fields and no `-X` from a subagent; unusual spellings of `rm -rf` and absolute paths inside the worktree in the destructive defaults; links to a frozen file need Bash and are not followed by `pre-edit`).
**Skipped / not checked:** not run on macOS or Linux (S-08's matrix will) · the hooks have not yet run inside a live Claude Code session on this repository; every test drives them through the CLI with Claude Code's documented JSON · the no-verify flag no longer bypasses the protected-branch check (REQ-3.9); `ALLOW_PROTECTED_COMMIT=1` is the one escape · the subagent marker now lives under the git common directory and is written by S-07's `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop`; until S-07 lands, the "git from a subagent" rule is tested with a seeded marker only · S-05's queue row still reads `PR #5`: `status --sync` promotes only `ready` slices, and S-05 merged straight from draft (a later slice teaches sync to record that) · no CI on this pull request yet.
